papers.title_en: SVG-Score: Human-Aligned Evaluation of Text-to-SVG Generation
papers.authors: Marco Cipriano, Leonardo Zini, Alexandra Schild, Valentin Teutschbein, Afsana Mimi, Marcella Cornia, Lorenzo Baraldi, Gerard de Melo
papers.evidence: 面向生成视觉内容的人类对齐评估框架，针对CLIP指标失效问题。
papers.tldr: 文本到SVG生成缺乏专门评估指标，现有CLIPScore等针对自然图像，对颜色、数量、空间关系等错误不敏感。本文提出SVG-Score框架：通过扰动实验暴露问题，构建人类标注的语义对齐数据集，并开发两种评估器——适配并对齐人类偏好的CLIP评分器用于快速评测，以及经监督微调和奖励强化学习的VLM评判器用于精细评估。在独立描述集上对主流生成器进行了基准测试。
papers.abstract_en: Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG) generation is attracting increasing attention as generative models improve in expressiveness and controllability. Progress, however, is held back by the lack of domain-specific evaluation protocols: current practice relies on metrics designed for natural images, most notably CLIPScore, which was never trained on vector graphics and aligns only partially with human judgment. We introduce \textbf{\ours}, a human-aligned evaluation framework for text-to-SVG generation. Through controlled caption and image perturbations, we first show that CLIP-based scores barely react to the errors SVG generators actually make, such as wrong colors, counts, and spatial relations, and that off-the-shelf Vision-Language Model (VLM) judges, while more sensitive, respond unevenly across error types and SVG styles. We then introduce a human-annotated dataset for \textit{Semantic Alignment}, measuring how faithfully a generated SVG reflects its caption. Building on it, we develop two complementary evaluators: CLIP scorers adapted to vector graphics and then aligned to human preferences, for fast large-scale evaluation, and a VLM judge trained with supervised fine-tuning and reward-shaped reinforcement learning, for more expressive and interpretable assessment. Using both, we benchmark major open-source, commercial, and optimization-based SVG generators on an independent caption set.
